sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Language descriptions: only the Glottolog stub. Other: Ethnologue and LINGUIST List entries. No primary texts, no lexicon, no archived recordings, nothing from SIL or PARADISEC.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 'Language resources: Nothing yet available or materials are not yet processed.' No SIL publication or survey listed for Koiwat.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid koiw1243 + reference records 38295 (Staalsen 1975) and 318703 (Haberland 1963).
sources.note: Bibliographic record only. Glottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist. Staalsen 1975 typed 'overview;wordlist' (Anthropos 70:6-16, covers Sengo, Burui, Gaikwundi, Sos Kundi, Koiwat, Iatmul dialects); Haberland 1963 = unpublished Frobenius-Institut Nachlass wordlists ('Kamangauwi' list = Koiwat). Zero descriptive references.

sources.citation: Search-engine and API search: ANU Open Research DSpace ('Koiwat', 'Sawos'), archive.org advanced search, Crossref, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Google Books, Bing, DuckDuckGo, JSTOR, HathiTrust full-text search, PARADISEC catalog.
sources.note: ANU: 'Koiwat' hits only Laycock 1973. archive.org: only Wikipedia-article PDFs, no Rosetta Project item for kxt. Crossref: no Staalsen 1975 record. OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Google Books: not reachable by automated download. Bing: bot filler unrelated to the query. JSTOR, HathiTrust, PARADISEC: an automated-access block/JS challenge. DuckDuckGo: timeout.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en): 'Koiwat language' stub; 'Ndu languages'; and the Sos Kundi, Gaikundi, Sawos (redirect), Burui, Sengo, Keak, Kwasengen, Sepik languages pages (wikitext downloaded 2026-09-17).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Koiwat stub: villages and coordinates only, cites Ethnologue 25 and a UN village gazetteer. Ndu page: Usher (2020) groups Boiken-Koiwat; general Ndu vowel remarks (Iatmul-based); nothing on stress and no Koiwat data. Sibling stubs contain no phonology.

sources.citation: Endangered Languages Project, 'Koiwat [aka Sawos]', entry 10612 (Internet Archive copy 2025-08-10).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Notes Koiwat is included within Laycock's (1973) 'Sawos', classification follows Staalsen (1975); ~450 speakers (1972) in Koiwat, Kamangaui, Seraba, Paiambi villages. Cites only Staalsen 1975, Ethnologue 18, Glottolog 2.3.

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul (ed.). 2009. Ethnologue 16, entry Koiwat (Internet Archive copy 2011-12-16); current ethnologue.com page blocked (not reachable by automated download).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Population 800 (2000 census); Ambunti District, between Munguma and Nagam rivers; Koiwat, Kamangaui, Seraba, Paiambit villages; classification Sepik, Ndu. Nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Aikhenvald, Alexandra Y. 2008. The Manambu language of East Sepik, Papua New Guinea. Oxford: Oxford University Press. Chapter 1 (Introduction), section 1.1 and note 3 on the Ndu family and the 'Sawos' varieties.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: classification remark only: 'Koiwat.. is lexically close to Boikin; whether or not it is a separate language requires further study'; no stress or tone statement for Koiwat (the Manambu stress description elsewhere in the book concerns Manambu only)

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Entry 91 SAWOS, printed pp.27-28 (PDF 31-32): Koiwat, Kamangaui, Seraba, Piambit listed as Sawos villages, Koiwat = 'dialect (4)'; 'No real dialect surveys have been undertaken, and there may be at least two distinct languages subsumed under Sawos'. Village index p.100: Kawat = Koiwat. Checklist only: no phonology, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1965. The Ndu language family (Sepik District, New Guinea). Pacific Linguistics C-1. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accent Koiwat, Kamangaui, Paiambit/Piambit, Seraba/Sarapa: zero hits. Section 14 'Notes on the Sawos language' treats Sawos as possibly not a separate language; no Koiwat data, no stress statement for any Sawos variety (the phonology chapters cover Wosera Abelam, Iatmul, Manambu etc.).

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of the Sepik-Ramu basin and environs. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The languages and linguistics of the New Guinea area, 197-432. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.

sources.citation: Staalsen, Philip. 1975. The languages of the Sawos region (New Guinea). Anthropos 70(1/2): 6-16.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher (DOI); library e-access not checked
sources.note: The only published primary data on Koiwat (SIL survey wordlists and lexicostatistics of the Sawos region incl. Koiwat, Kamangaui, Seraba, Paiambit). Glottolog types it wordlist-only; a stress statement is unlikely, but it is the sole place stress could be marked in transcription and it may name any further SIL manuscript on Koiwat.

sources.citation: Haberland, Eike. 1963. Verschiedene Sprachen aus oberem Korowori und Gegend (ms. wordlists; list 'Kamangauwi' = Koiwat). Nachlass Haberland, Frobenius-Institut, Frankfurt.
